persona.name: Naomi Kirishima

occupation.title: HR Planning Group Manager
occupation.organization: A 12,000-employee electronics manufacturer headquartered in Yokohama, Kanagawa
occupation.description: Runs organizational development and internal communication policy for a sprawling enterprise. Her weeks hold 12-18 meetings: labor-management councils, promotion committees, harassment case reviews — exactly the meetings where what is said and what is meant diverge most. She is a key influencer in the company's ringi process for any tool touching employee data, though the final stamp belongs to the CHRO and IT.

persona.education: Psychology degree from Ochanomizu University; labor management certification (sharoushi study, uncompleted — a private sore spot) and an executive HR program at Keio.
long_term_goals: Become the company's first female HR division director
Rebuild the manager-training system she inherited
Protect the informal channels where employees actually tell the truth
Take her mother to Vienna for the New Year concert someday
persona.style: Measured and precise, with the diplomatic register of someone who writes sensitive personnel announcements for a living. She asks second-order questions — not 'does it transcribe well?' but 'what happens to candor when people know they're transcribed?'. Her disagreement arrives wrapped as a thoughtful concern, which makes it more dangerous, and she knows it.

traits: Skeptical of technological fixes for human problems
Slow to trust vendors, slower to forgive breaches

interests: How recording changes what people say in meetings (honne vs tatemae)
Works council and labor-law implications of monitoring tools
likes: Meetings where someone finally says the real thing
dislikes: The phrase 'AI will capture everything' said approvingly
Managers who outsource listening to a transcript
Leaked personnel information, above all else
Vendors who demo with fake harassment-case examples

beliefs: The most important sentence in a Japanese meeting is the one spoken after the recorder stops
A perfect record of tatemae is a perfectly useless record
HR's job is to know things that must never be searchable
skills: Briefing executives on what they don't want to hear

general: Bans recording in personnel-related meetings, allows it elsewhere case by case
Takes her own shorthand notes and shreds drafts
Interviews employees over coffee, never in bookable rooms with glass walls
Reads vendor privacy policies for what they omit

morning: 6:15 wake, 20 minutes of piano practice with headphones
Tokyu line commute reading HR law newsletters
workday: Committee meetings, case reviews, and one-on-ones
Writes policy documents in the quiet hour after 18:00
evening: Home by 20:00, cooks while listening to concert recordings
One episode of something undemanding, asleep by 23:30
weekend: Saturday: gallery or concert with her sister
Sunday: meal prep and a long walk along the Tsurumi River

health.physical: Healthy; tension headaches during shunto (spring labor negotiation) season.
health.mental: Composed but carries the accumulated weight of other people's worst workplace days; sees a counselor quarterly and tells no one.

relationships.name: Mari
relationships.description: A freelance illustrator in Koenji; the one person with whom Naomi is unguarded and silly.

relationships.name: Sudo-CHRO
relationships.description: Enthusiastic about AI tools in a way she finds naive; managing his enthusiasm is an unlisted part of her job.
